question.problem:
The results of a group of students on an algebra test are normally distributed with a mean of $75$ and a variance of $125$, while the results of the same group on a geometry test are normally distributed with a mean of $62$ and a variance of $110.$ 
If one student is randomly selected, what is the probability that they scored higher on the algebra test? You may assume that the student's scores on both tests are independent. 

*Hint: A table of values of $Φ(z)$ for different values of $z$ is given below, where $Φ(z)$ is the cumulative distribution function for the standard normal distribution. *

| $z$ | $\,0.04\,$ | $\,0.05\,$ | $\,0.06\,$ | $\,0.07\,$ | $\,0.08\,$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $\,-0.8\,$ | $\,0.2005\,$ | $\,0.1977\,$ | $\,0.1949\,$ | $\,0.1922\,$ | $\,0.1894\,$ |
| $\,-0.7\,$ | $\,0.2296\,$ | $\,0.2266\,$ | $\,0.2236\,$ | $\,0.2206\,$ | $\,0.2177\,$ |
| $\,-0.6\,$ | $\,0.2611\,$ | $\,0.2578\,$ | $\,0.2546\,$ | $\,0.2514\,$ | $\,0.2483\,$ |
question.worked_solution:
Let $X$ denote the student's algebra test result, and let $Y$ denote the student's geometry result. We want to find 

$$
P(X>Y)=P(X-Y>0).
$$

Since $X$ and $Y$ are  independent random variables such that $X∼N(75,125)$ and $Y∼N(62,110)$, then 

$$
\begin{aligned}X-Y & ∼N(75-62,125+110) \\  & ∼N(13,235).\end{aligned}
$$

 
So, the variable $X-Y$ is normally distributed with mean $\mu =13$ and standard deviation $\sigma =\sqrt{235}.$

In order to find $P(X-Y>0),$ we convert $X-Y$ to a standard normal random variable by $z$-scoring:
    

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X-Y>0) & =P(Z>\frac{0-13}{\sqrt{235}}) \\  & ≈P(Z>-0.85) \\  & =1-Φ(-0.85)\end{aligned}
$$

Using the $z$-table, we see that

$$
Φ(-0.85)≈0.1977.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X-Y>0) & ≈1-Φ(-0.85) \\  & ≈1-0.1977 \\  & =0.8023.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we conclude that the probability that the student scored higher on the algebra test is $0.8023.$
